description: A groundwater well database for Brazil (GWDBrazil) is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by José Gescilam S. M. Uchôa et al. Sufficient spatiotemporal in-situ groundwater-level measurements can inform sustainable water management. Despite their importance, lack of harmonized, quality-controlled datasets has hindered large-scale groundwater studies in Brazil. Coverage: national (BR); published in 2025. Formats: CSV, Excel, NetCDF, Shapefile. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support water-network, drainage and hydraulic studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
